pr_8666.test_xml: Both XML artifacts contain only the shard-level timeout (exit code 142); no assertion traceback or active test name.
pr_8666.container_logs: Electric connected to Postgres and began shape replication on both shards. PostgreSQL logs include permission denied for database postgres while creating a publication, then successful replication slot startup; this is not enough to attribute the timeout.
pr_8666.http2_ingress: Shard 1 log contains normal page asset responses. Shard 2 shows page and sync requests with HTTP 200, two GET /actions/stream?state=decision_pending responses of HTTP 503 at 21:33:08 and 21:33:10 UTC, then further sync requests returning HTTP 200 through 21:33:12. No browser HAR/trace exists for the in-progress test because those artifacts are emitted by teardown.

pr_8823.historical_error: mirror.gcr.io returned HTTP 404 for a Postgres layer blob.
pr_8823.interpretation: The exact blob is currently available at both registries; this does not establish its availability at the historical failure time.

interpretation_limits: GitHub attempt-specific API exposes actor accounts but not whether the rerun was initiated via UI or API, nor the actor's motive.
The elapsed 20m34s and 26m53s gaps between failed jobs and rerun attempts do not identify their cause.
The BuildBuddy logs prove three automatic remote-execution transport retries during PR 8666 attempt 2; they do not expose the internal retry policy or prove retry-budget exhaustion.
The timed-out Pytest logs are quiet and artifacts from the active test's teardown are absent, so the failing test case and assertion-level cause remain unknown.
